defects.summary: A second VS Code window is running concurrent agent threads against D:/Freelance/Claw. Feature work is isolated in its own worktree, so commits here are unaffected, but do not run git ops in the main worktree while it is active.

A manual model choice in the composer is not always honoured. With clawAI.routingMode left at its AUTO default, runs execute on whatever the backend router selects while the status bar and composer both display the manually chosen model. Observed: composer and status bar showed kimi-k2.7-code while chat-service logged callProvider provider=OLLAMA model=deepseek-v4-pro with usedFallback=false. deepseek-v4-pro could not emit a valid Runtime Protocol 2.0 tool object, so five consecutive edits failed as MODEL_TOOL_REQUEST_UNREPAIRABLE and read as an output-token problem rather than a routing one.
defects.evidence: docker logs claw-chat-service | grep callProvider - 50 dispatches to deepseek-v4-pro during the failing window

defects.summary: workspace.files update rewrites an entire file, so editing any file over roughly 8 KB overflows the model output budget and fails the run. patch with a small anchored hunk succeeds on the same file. The tool guidance does not warn the model away from update on large files, and the truncation error blames output length without naming the operation that caused it.
defects.evidence: Repeated MODEL_TOOL_REQUEST_UNREPAIRABLE on an 8.2 KB repository file; identical edit succeeded once the model was told to use patch with a three-line anchor and forbidden from using update.

defects.summary: Two VS Code windows against the same serve-web server cannot both hold a ClawAI session. Connecting the second window silently logs the first out, and reconnecting the first logs the second out, so parallel agent threads are not possible. The evicted window shows the Connect gate again with no explanation and any queued message is lost.
defects.evidence: Windows on pages 2 and 3 of the same browser, same backend; each reconnect evicted the other. Neither queued task ran.

defects.summary: The running chat-service image was stale. HARD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS was still 16384 in the container while source had 32768, because chat-service runs a baked prod image with no source mount and had not been rebuilt since the fix landed on main at 10:36. Every agent edit truncated mid tool-object against a ceiling that was already fixed on disk. Rebuilt and recreated chat-service; two patches then landed in a single turn.
defects.evidence: docker exec claw-chat-service grep HARD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS dist -> 16384 before rebuild, 32768 after. Five consecutive MODEL_TOOL_REQUEST_UNREPAIRABLE failures before, none after.

Rebuilt packages/shared-types and restarted auth-service.

verifiedFindings: ConnectorModel unique key is @@unique([connectorId, modelKey]); provider is fixed per Connector, so the same modelKey under two connectors is two rows.
connector-models.repository.ts replaceMany HARD-DELETES any model absent from the incoming sync (modelKey notIn), destroying history on one bad provider response. Pack forbids this.
GET /connectors/:id/models has no @RequirePermissions while every sibling route requires ADMIN_CONNECTORS_MANAGE.
PlanModelAccess (auth-service) stores provider/model as free strings with no relation to ConnectorModel (connector-service); nothing validates an assignment against synced inventory.
entitlements.service.ts resolveModelAccessMode returns ALLOW_ALL for any admin; non-admins default to DENY_ALL (fail-closed default, verified).
applyPlanModelGate treats an EMPTY allowedModels array as unrestricted allow-all, by design comment - so a plan with zero rows grants every model.
access-control.service.ts assertCanUseCritic and assertResearchAccess return early with an explicit // fail-open comment when entitlements are null. Pack requires fail-closed.
Two independent gates already exist: applyPlanModelGate (routing-service) and AccessControlService.assertModelAllowed (chat-service). Neither consults connector inventory; both trust plan rows.

policy.gates: ONE run at the very end of the flagship only. No per-edit or per-batch lint/test/build.
policy.commandApproval: supervisor approves every terminal command; gate commands rejected until the end

knownCeiling: A coding-agent run is bounded at ~100 tool calls: maxModelTurns and maxToolRounds are debited 1:1 per invocation and both are capped at 100 by the protocol schema in BOTH repos, so ULTRA maxToolCalls 250 is unreachable. Every batch must be scoped to fit well under 100 tool calls. Raising it needs a coordinated protocol change in claw-coding-agent and claw-chat-service.
method: The agent ignores prompt-level tool budgets and dies at ~100 model turns. Discovery-shaped tasks fail. Working shape: supervisor names an exact short read list, agent traces and authors. Confirmed on batch 1a.
adrCorrections: ADR proposed an exposure enum containing DEPRECATED; dropped, because ModelLifecycle already owns DEPRECATED and SUNSET and two enums encoding the same concept produce contradictory states.

ADR proposed a foreign key from PlanModelAccess to ConnectorModel; impossible, they live in different service databases and this repository forbids crossing a service database boundary. The link must be a plain column validated over HTTP.
openCaveats: Exposure is enforced on the manual send path. AUTO goes through the routing gate, which is plan-aware but not yet exposure-aware; the catalog it routes over is exposure-filtered, so the remaining gap is a crafted AUTO request naming an unexposed model.
No admin exposure UI (batch 6) and the plan editor still offers free text (batch 8).
workingTechnique: For any edit to a file larger than about 8 KB: instruct patch with a minimal anchored hunk (quote the exact 3 trailing lines) and explicitly forbid update. Verify the executed model with: docker logs claw-chat-service | grep callProvider.
parallelismNote: Parallel agent threads are not viable (CA-06). Execute serially in one window; use the waiting time for supervisor verification rather than a second thread.
provenanceNote: chat-messages.service.ts publish wiring (4 mechanical edits) was applied by the supervisor after the agent failed the anchors repeatedly on that ~1900-line file. Design and every other change in this batch are agent-authored.
